messages:
Maya: quick sync — thinking about slicing tenant capacity by observed SLAs instead of static quotas. sketch below, want thoughts.

Kevin: what's the main trigger? fairness hits in prod or cost/efficiency?

Maya: both. large tenants keep consuming burst credits and we see tail latency regressions for small customers during spikes. static per-tenant quotas are too blunt.

Liang: high-level idea: compute a short window (30s) SLA score per tenant (based on p99 latency and error rate) and derive a dynamic weight w. allocate reservoir shards proportional to w, with a min_share floor.

Sam: sounds promising but gaming worry: if weight is computed from recent success, a client could oscillate patterns to get more share. do we have anti-gaming controls?

Maya: yep — plan includes a separate abuse_detector that ingests traffic features (rate of short-lived retries, header fuzzing, unusual token patterns) and can multiply weight by an abuse_multiplier in [0,1]. detection runs asynchronously so it can't be trivially spoofed per-request.

Kevin: what about placement? central controller gives consistent slices but adds round-trip to apply updates. local edge enforcement is faster but risks divergence. tradeoffs?

Liang: propose hybrid: local fast-path enforces a soft token-bucket sized from last-known weight; reconcile every 15s with central. central can issue hard overrides on detected abuse or when global capacity shifts.

deploy-bot: note: canary plan recommended — controller + local shim to 5% traffic, monitor spillover and p99.

Maya: config sketch:
```json
{
  "slice_window": "30s",
  "stability_alpha": "0.2",    // EWMA smoothing for weight updates
  "min_share": "0.02",         // minimum fraction of reservoir per tenant
  "reconcile_interval": "15s",
  "abuse_multiplier_ttl": "60s"
}
```

Sam: observability requirements: token-level p99, spillover_rate, abuse_score_histogram, reconciliation_lag. set alert when spillover_rate > 2% or reconciliation_lag > 30s. also record events when multiplier applied.

Kevin: implementation note: to avoid thrash, we need deterministic tie-breaker when weights are very close: prefer tenant with lower recent burst_use. also cap per-update change (delta_max = 20%).

Liang: performance sims: we should run 1000-tenant synthetic workloads with 1% heavy hitters and measure tail latency and fairness index (Jain). I'll add sim harness to RFC.

Maya: next steps: I'll draft RFC with metric goals, sim results, rollout plan (canary -> 20% -> global) and rollback hooks. please DM if you want to co-author.

Kevin: +1 to metrics-first RFC. count me in for the canary runbook.

Sam: happy to help on abuse-detector heuristics and alerting thresholds.

Maya: thanks — will ping when draft is up.
